title: Avoid rolling over twice in searchable snapshot test

timeline.message:
Avoid rolling over twice in searchable snapshot test

Manually rolling over the data stream was 1. not necessary, and
2. causing issues when it happened after ILM had already rolled
over, which would make ILM convert the second backing index into a
searchable snapshot as well, possibly preventing the data stream
from being deleted.

Fixes #107421
timeline.author: Niels Bauman

timeline.body:
Manually rolling over the data stream was 1. not necessary, and
2. causing issues when it happened after ILM had already rolled over, which would make ILM convert the second backing index into a searchable snapshot as well, possibly preventing the data stream from being deleted.

Fixes #107421
Should we check this before we index the document? The chances it will rollover so quickly is unlikely but better to be sure right?

reply.body: Ah yeah I think I thought about that but concluded that this was fine as `backingIndices.get(0)` would point to the same index before and after rollover, but I forgot to take into account that the searchable snapshot action removes the original index, of course. Good suggestion, will do :+1:

Ah no nvm, I remember why I didn't move the check before the document indexation; the data stream doesn't exist yet before the document is indexed :smile:. I'll move the check and add a `PUT _data_stream/...` request.

timeline.body: LGTM, since we rely on ILM to do the rollover, I think we should move all the pre-rollover checks earlier to avoid any timing issues.

timeline.author: Niels Bauman

+    private static class NonDynamicFieldMapper extends FieldMapper {
+        private static final String NAME = "non_dynamic";
+
+        private static final TypeParser PARSER = new TypeParser(

+            List.of(notFromDynamicTemplates(NAME), notInMultiFields(NAME))
+        );
+
+        private static class Builder extends FieldMapper.Builder {
+            private final Parameter<Map<String, String>> meta = Parameter.metaParam();

+            Builder(String name) {

+            protected Parameter<?>[] getParameters() {
+                return new Parameter<?>[] { meta };
+            }
